The Azure resources are in [[zwa.azure-dlp-integration.resources]], the Filewatcher VM in [[zwa.azure-dlp-integration.filewatcher]], the Cloud-to-Cloud path in [[zwa.azure-dlp-integration.cloud-to-cloud]] and the integration lifecycle in [[zwa.azure-dlp-integration.management]]. Where the incidents then appear is [[zwa.incidents]]. The ZIA-side Azure forwarding setup is in [[zia.dlp.cloud-to-cloud-forwarding]] and the Incident Receiver setup for Azure VMs in [[zia.dlp.incident-receiver]]. The API, SDKs and Terraform are unread {{gap:other-sources-unchecked}}.

checks.do: Which method the integration uses: Zscaler Incident Receiver or Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding.

Whether the NAT Gateway IPs of the Workflow Automation cloud are allowed on the storage account (always, per the intro page; when the storage account is restricted to selected IP addresses, per the Incident Receiver page), and whether the Zscaler Hub IP addresses are accepted for the ZIA-side Cloud-to-Cloud forwarding.
Whether Validate passed, and whether the integration was disabled and re-enabled after wrong values were corrected; the pages differ on whether the values are corrected before or after the disable.
Whether read access to the data blob was enabled when the resource manager stack was created, if Hide Evidence Data or Hide Trigger Data is disabled.

methods.statement: Workflow Automation's DLP application integration with Azure uses Zscaler incident forwarding methods to send information about policy violations to the organization's Azure storage containers, and can be configured with either Zscaler Incident Receiver or Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding.

quotes: You must configure Workflow Automation integration with the Azure instance using Zscaler incident forwarding methods to allow the Zscaler service to send information about policy violations to public cloud storage (i.e., to your organization's Azure storage containers).
You can configure DLP application integration with Azure using one of the following methods:
- Zscaler Incident Receiver
- Cloud-to-Cloud Incident Forwarding

nat-gateway-ips.statement: The Azure introduction page says the NAT Gateway IPs of the organization's Workflow Automation cloud must be allowed on the Azure storage account; the cloud is identified from the admin login URL (that page's example: logging in at https://app.us1.zsworkflow.net/ gives the cloud produs1). Separately, the ZIA-side Cloud-to-Cloud page says the storage account must be accessible to the necessary IP addresses and points to Zscaler Hub IP Addresses for them.

quotes: To view the various IP addresses of different Workflow Automation clouds associated with Zscaler, see NAT Gateway IP addresses. Ensure that these NAT Gateway IPs are allowed on the storage account.
if you log in to https://app.us1.zsworkflow.net/, then that organization's cloud is produs1.
You need to make sure your storage account is accessible to the necessary IP addresses. To do so, go to Security + networking > Networking.
To learn which IP addresses to connect to, see Zscaler Hub IP Addresses.

zir-path-overview.statement: To configure the Azure DLP application integration with Zscaler Incident Receiver (ZIR), a ZIR Azure instance must be deployed; it lets the organization receive DLP incident metadata files and the evidence file from ZIR and upload them to its Azure storage containers.

quotes: To configure Workflow Automation DLP application integration using Zscaler Incident Receiver (ZIR), you must deploy a ZIR Azure instance.

Doing so enables your organization to receive Data Loss Prevention (DLP) incident metadata files and the evidence file from ZIR and upload them to your organization's Azure storage containers in your Azure account.

who-can-configure.statement: Super admins, and admins with Full or Restricted access to Workflow Automation, can configure the DLP Azure application integration, which must be configured before the organization's DLP incidents are available on the Incidents page.

quotes: Super admins or admins with Full or Restricted access to Workflow Automation can configure the DLP Azure application integration.
Before your organization's DLP incidents are available for review and remediation on the Incidents page in the Zscaler Admin Console, the DLP Azure application integration must be configured.

required-outputs.statement: Adding a DLP Azure application integration on the Integrations dashboard needs values from the Azure stack creation (or manual creation): TenantId, applicationClientId, applicationClientSecret, storageAccountName and the system topic resource ID.

quotes: Various outputs (TenantId, applicationClientId, applicationClientSecret, storageAccountName, and systemTopicResource ID) from the stack creation or manually created are required to add a DLP Azure application integration on the Integrations dashboard in Workflow Automation.

custom-storage-endpoint.statement: The Custom Storage Endpoint URL field of the DLP Azure integration is optional: it takes a URL in the format https://<custom endpoint> when Workflow Automation should not use the default public endpoint, and is left blank to use the public endpoint.

quotes: Custom Storage Endpoint URL: (Optional) If you do not want Workflow Automation to access the storage account through a default public endpoint, enter a custom storage endpoint URL in the format https://<custom endpoint>. If you want to use a public endpoint, leave the field blank.

validate-before-add.statement: Validate checks the account credentials entered for the Azure integration and the format of the Event Grid System Topic Resource ID, and the integration can only be added if it passes; if validation fails or wrong values were saved, the Incident Receiver page says you must disable the integration, correct the values and re-enable it.

quotes: The system validates the account credentials that are entered with the Azure integration.
It also checks whether the format is correct for the Event Grid System Topic Resource Id. You can only add the integration if it passes validation.
If the validation fails for any reason, or if the configuration has been created or updated with the wrong values,
you must disable the integration, correct the values for the integration, and re-enable it.

privacy-hide-defaults.statement: In the Privacy Settings section of the DLP Azure integration, Hide Evidence Data and Hide Trigger Data are selected by default for admins, end users and managers/approvers, and Hide Policy Details is not selected by default for admins but is selected by default for end users and managers/approvers.

quotes: Hide Evidence Data - Admin: Select if you do not want admins to be able to generate presigned evidence links for an incident on the Violation Content tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can generate evidence links. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Trigger Data - Admin: Select if you do not want admins to be able to see the trigger data for an incident on the Violation Content tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can see the trigger data. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details - Admin: Select if you do not want the admins to be able to view any of the policy details for the incident on the Violation Details tab of the Incident Details drawer. Otherwise, they can view the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is not selected by default.

Hide Evidence Data - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to generate presigned evidence links for an incident. Otherwise, they can generate evidence links. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Trigger Data - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to see the trigger data for an incident. Otherwise, they can see the trigger data. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to view any of the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Evidence Data - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to generate presigned evidence links for the incident. Otherwise, they can generate evidence links. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Trigger Data - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to see the trigger data for the incident. Otherwise, they can see the trigger data. This checkbox is selected by default.

Hide Policy Details - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to view the policy details for the incident. Otherwise, they can view the policy details for the incident. This checkbox is selected by default.

privacy-non-triggered.statement: The Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches checkboxes (Admin, End User, Manager/Approver) hide the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries and Other Matched Rules sections of the policy details, and each is only available when the matching Hide Policy Details checkbox is not selected; the Admin one is not selected by default.

quotes: Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - Admin: Select if you do not want the admins to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident on the Violation Details tab of the Incident Details drawer.
This checkbox is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - Admin checkbox. This checkbox is not selected by default.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - End User: Select if you do not want the end users responding to an incident notification to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident.
This checkbox is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - End User checkbox.

Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches - Manager/Approver: Select if you do not want the approvers or managers responding to an incident escalation notification to be able to view the Non-Triggered Engines and Dictionaries section and the Other Matched Rules section of the policy details for the incident.
This checkbox is only available if you do not select the Hide Policy Details - Manager/Approver checkbox.

privacy-read-access-dependency.statement: If Hide Evidence Data or Hide Trigger Data is disabled in the integration but read access to the data blob was not enabled when creating the resource manager stack, no one can generate evidence links or view trigger data in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: If you disable Hide Evidence Data or Hide Trigger Data in the integration, but you did not enable read access to the data blob when creating the resource manager stack, no one can generate evidence links or view trigger data in the Zscaler Admin Console.

cloud-url-example.summary: The Azure introduction page's example login URL for identifying the cloud differs from the Incident Receiver page's example.

quotes: if you log in to https://app.us1.zsworkflow.net/, then that organization's cloud is produs1.

positions.says: Logging in at app.us1.zsworkflow.net gives the cloud produs1.

quotes: For example, if you log in to https://app.produs1.zsworkflow.net/, then that organization's cloud is produs1.

positions.says: Logging in at app.produs1.zsworkflow.net gives the cloud produs1.

cloud-url-example.impact: The cloud name produs1 is the same in both, but the login hostname differs (us1 versus produs1), so the pages do not settle which hostname admins of that cloud use; read the cloud from the tenant's own login URL.

nat-allowlist-conditional.summary: The Azure introduction page states the NAT Gateway IP allowlisting unconditionally, but the Incident Receiver page applies it only when the storage account is restricted to selected IP addresses.

quotes: Ensure that these NAT Gateway IPs are allowed on the storage account.

positions.says: The NAT Gateway IPs must be allowed on the storage account, with no condition.

quotes: If you want to restrict the storage account to selected IP addresses (i.e., if you select true for this field), then you must allowlist the IP addresses associated with your Workflow Automation cloud to communicate with the storage account.

positions.says: The allowlisting is required only if the storage account is restricted to selected IP addresses; the note says 'this field' under the Create Private DNS Zone parameter and names no other toggle.

nat-allowlist-conditional.impact: Whether an unrestricted storage account also needs the allowlisting is not settled; which template parameter 'this field' refers to is not named (see zwa.azure-dlp-integration.resources).

reenable-order.summary: The Incident Receiver and Cloud-to-Cloud pages say to disable, correct and re-enable the integration after a failed validation; the Azure managing page says to disable and re-enable it after correcting the values.

quotes: you must disable the integration, correct the values for the integration, and re-enable it.

positions.says: Disable the integration, correct the values, then re-enable it (the Cloud-to-Cloud page words it the same way).

quotes: you must disable and re-enable the integration after you correct the values for the integration.
evidence.after: To edit a DLP Azure application integration in Workflow Automation:

positions.says: Disable and re-enable the integration after correcting the values.

reenable-order.impact: Whether the values are corrected before or after the disable is not settled; the shared requirement is that the integration is disabled and re-enabled once the values are right.

non-triggered-defaults.title: What are the defaults of the End User and Manager/Approver Hide Policy Details for Non-Triggered Matches checkboxes?
non-triggered-defaults.detail: Only the Admin checkbox says 'not selected by default'; the End User and Manager/Approver ones state no default on the captured Incident Receiver page.

other-sources-unchecked.title: What do the Workflow Automation API, SDKs and Terraform say about the Azure integration?
other-sources-unchecked.detail: This subject covers the Azure configuration and management pages; the Workflow Automation API reference, the Python and Go SDKs and Terraform for these integration objects were not read. The ZIA-side forwarding setup for Microsoft Azure and the Incident Receiver setup for Azure VMs are in zia.dlp.cloud-to-cloud-forwarding and zia.dlp.incident-receiver.
